title: Exercise Northstar: D-30
description: Thirty days to build a live command screen for the SAF's biggest exercise.
storyContext: Classified briefing. In 30 days the SAF launches Exercise Northstar, its biggest this decade. Command wants one live screen: every unit's position, supplies, comms — working in jungle with barely any signal.

callbacks.arc1-ch1:serverless: That serverless setup from NDP? It's why Command picked your team — "get us whoever ran the parade app."

software-engineer.title: Design the Command Screen
software-engineer.instruction: One screen, everything at once. Critical info centre-stage, details on side panels, light status below.
software-engineer.hint: What gets checked every few seconds earns the most space.
software-engineer.consequenceSuccess: The layout clicks. A colonel squints at the demo: "Finally. One screen that makes sense."
software-engineer.consequenceFail: Commanders hunt through panels for the map. In a crisis, seconds of hunting cost plenty. Reshuffle time.

data-scientist.title: Handle the Data Flow
data-scientist.instruction: Field units ping positions every 30 seconds — thousands of updates a minute. How do you turn that into a screen?
data-scientist.hint: Does a 5-second delay actually matter? Does bad data?

options.label: Process every update instantly. Real-time screen, heavy computing — one bad reading can glitch the display.
options.consequence: The screen dances in real time. Then one corrupted ping draws a tank in the ocean. Fun.

options.label: Collect updates every 5 seconds, clean them, then display. Slightly delayed, never wrong.
options.consequence: Five-second-old positions, zero garbage on screen. Nobody ever notices the delay. Clean wins.

options.label: Each device crunches its own data, sends a summary. Cuts radio use 80%; loses raw detail.
options.consequence: Radio traffic drops 80% — huge in the jungle. The analysts grumble about missing raw data.

options.label: Critical alerts instantly, the rest in 10-second bundles. Balanced, but more parts to maintain.
options.consequence: Best of both worlds — and twice the moving parts. Future-you inherits the maintenance manual.

cloud-engineer.title: Set Up the Field Network
cloud-engineer.instruction: Patchy jungle signal. Build a reliable link from field to command screen. Order the steps.
cloud-engineer.hint: Find the dead zones before you build. Test before D-Day.

items.label: Walk the ground to find dead zones
Place portable relay nodes at key positions
Add a satellite link as backup
Test data speed from the furthest point
Make devices auto-switch to the best network

cloud-engineer.consequenceSuccess: Signal holds from the deepest valley to the command post. The comms sergeant salutes your relay map.
cloud-engineer.consequenceFail: You place relays before finding the dead zones — three end up useless. The jungle wins round one.
